selected_primary_idea.title: GigaCascade: Fossil-Anchored Causal Comparison of Constraint Release in Sauropod Gigantism
selected_primary_idea.scientific_object: Repeated extreme body-mass evolution among sauropodomorph dinosaurs
selected_primary_idea.central_hypothesis: Extreme sauropod body mass became evolutionarily accessible when feeding architecture, axial pneumaticity, growth/life-history capacity, and ecological opportunity jointly crossed lineage-specific feasibility thresholds; an interaction model should predict held-out giant lineages better than any single-factor or additive alternative.
mechanism: Long neck and reduced oral processing may increase accessible forage volume and intake opportunity.
Axial pneumaticity may relax mass-distribution constraints and records a respiratory anatomical system, without directly measuring physiology.
Rapid tissue deposition and oviparous life history may improve access to very large adult body size.
Ecological opportunity may modulate, rather than universally cause, the expression of these traits.
primary_predictions: A preregistered interaction model improves leave-clade-out prediction of giant-size transitions over climate-only, neck-only, pneumaticity-only, and additive models.
Candidate enabling traits precede or co-emerge with mass increases more often than expected under a shuffled-timing null.
The model remains directionally stable across alternative mass estimates, phylogenies, trait codings, and sampling weights.
falsification_conditions: No out-of-clade predictive advantage beyond neutral or single-factor models.
Temporal ordering fails for most independently giant lineages.
Apparent effects disappear under plausible fossil, phylogenetic, or sampling uncertainty.
A small number of exceptionally complete taxa explain the entire result.
selected_primary_idea.claim_ceiling: Conditional support for a macroevolutionary feasibility model; no direct measurement of extinct metabolism, behavior, or thermoregulation.
